top_signals.title: Nigeria’s Naira Weakens With Investors Wary of Election Upset
top_signals.summary: Nigeria’s naira is seeing increasing volatility as uncertainty over next year’s election and expectations of higher US interest rates see investors shift away from the West African nation.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Treasuries Slip as Huang’s Nvidia Return Revives Risk Trade
top_signals.summary: US Treasuries fell as Jensen Huang’s return to the helm of Nvidia Corp. revived demand for risk assets, unwinding some of the haven bid that had swept through the bond market during last week’s AI-fueled selloff.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin rebounds 17% from $55K lows as Nvidia rally sparks $500M crypto liquidations
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin price upside hit $64,500 as risk assets surged on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s reinstatement, while crypto liquidations topped $500 million four hours.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Digital asset volatility and institutional crypto positioning changes.

top_signals.title: Commission opens formal investigation into possible anticompetitive conduct by Coca-Cola Europacific Partners in the non-alcoholic drinks sector
top_signals.summary: European Commission Press release Brussels, 23 Nov 2026 The European Commission has opened a formal antitrust investigation to assess whether Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (‘CCEP') has breached EU competition rules by (i) hindering the cross-border trade of carbonated soft drinks and sports drinks; and (ii) denying certain wholesale customers the possibility to negotiate the procurement of these products on a multi-country basis.
